defect.problem: The good_law treatment field itself matches the lake record, but the page's categorical no-negative-treatment framing is too strong because the disclosed lake derivation contains proposed negative/questioned progeny and an explicit lane2 audit marker.
defect.proposed_fix: Retain field_i_validity: good_law, but soften the narrative to say the lake currently rates Mitchell good law and no confirmed overruling is disclosed; note that proposed negative progeny exists and lane2 audit remains required.

reasons: Lake treatment matches the page on field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 2019-06-27, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point false, and the plurality scope note.
However, disclosed progeny derivation is not clean: lane2_top_cited is capped, audit_needed is true, and proposed_negative_events is 20.
The lake edges are proposed and field_iii is mentioned, so they do not refute good_law, but they do refute an unqualified no-negative-treatment statement.
residual_risks: Resolving whether any proposed overruled/questioned edge is real negative treatment requires the pending treatment audit.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace categorical no-negative phrasing with a qualified current-status sentence tied to the lake good_law field and audit status.
